newsitem.title: FINLAND: SENTRA CEO CONFIDENT ON BALANCE SHEET.
newsitem.headline: SENTRA CEO CONFIDENT ON BALANCE SHEET.

text.p: Finnish retail group Sentra's balance sheet is still in good shape despite the purchase of Suomen Spar retail operations that will quintuple net sales, Sentra chief executive Bjorn Westerholm said on Tuesday.
"Before this deal, we did not have a single penny of debt, and the cash situation was excellent. And after the deal, the situation will still be strong," Westerholm said in an interview with Reuters.
Westerholm declined to comment in detail on debt or on the profit outlook for the new group, saying that his first word on that would be to a shareholders' meeting on February 26.

A week ago, Sentra bought 350 Spar shops and a 35 percent stake in wholesaler TukoSpar from Kesko-controlled Tuko for a total of 335 million markka. The deal is still subject to EU approval of the Kesko demerger plan.
The deal will boost annual net sales from about 800 million markka this year to about four billion markka.
